summary: The Hourglass Twins are a binary planet system orbiting very close to the Sun: Ember Twin (a desert world with deep caves) and Ash Twin (covered in sand over a rocky core). Sand flows between them like an hourglass over each 22-minute loop, revealing Ash Twin's Nomai warp towers and the Ash Twin Project hidden in its core.

biology: The Hourglass Twins are a binary planet system whose two members orbit each other.
The Hourglass Twins are the closest celestial bodies to the Sun, excluding the Interloper at its periapsis and the Sun Station.
Both planets have low gravity compared to Timber Hearth.
The semi-major axis of the Hourglass Twins' barycenter is approximately 5 km.
Ember Twin is primarily made of red canyons and cliffs with cacti and various rock formations on the surface.
Ember Twin has a wide equatorial canyon that divides the planet into two halves and leads down to its core.
Ember Twin is likely a former ocean world, evidenced by aquatic-animal and plant fossils in its caves and northern lakebed.
Ash Twin is initially covered with sand laid over a black rocky core.
Both planets orbit very close to the Sun.
behavior: The Twins' gravitational pull on each other changes periodically, causing sand to flow from one to the other over approximately 20 minutes like an hourglass.
At the start of each loop, all the sand is on Ash Twin.
Two minutes into each loop, Ember Twin begins pulling sand from Ash Twin.
Once the flow of sand stops, the current loop will soon end (the Sun supernovas).
By loop's end, all sand has filled Ember Twin's deep cave systems, while Ash Twin is reduced to a rocky core and a few skeletal stone pillars.
The pillar of sand does not damage the player directly, but can drag the player and their ship from Ash Twin up to Ember Twin.
If the player is caught in the sand pillar inside their ship on Ember Twin, they will be pinned to the ground and immobilized for the duration of being covered.
Ember Twin's interior caves and tunnels progressively fill with sand and become inaccessible as the loop progresses.
location: The Hourglass Twins are home to the traveler Chert.
Ember Twin has an intricate cave system with multiple entrances and Nomai structures.
Escape Pod 2 is embedded into Ember Twin's crust near the south pole and creates an opening into the Crash Site Caves beneath.
The Crash Site Caves under Escape Pod 2 contain trails of Nomai writing chronicling the survivors' arrival and pointing toward the Sunless City.
The Sunless City is a large ruined Nomai settlement in the cave systems of Ember Twin.
The Sunless City is built into a massive vertical cavern.
The Sunless City is divided into four districts: the Anglerfish Overlook District, the Stepping Stone District, the High Energy Lab Trailhead, and the Eye Shrine District.
The Sunless City's districts are connected by stairways and gravity lifts.
The Sunless City has a central hub built into the cavern wall with trees and a Nomai control panel that lights each district individually.
Erosion has opened holes in the Sunless City, causing it to flood with sand from bottom to top during each loop, sealing off districts and pathways.
The Anglerfish Overlook District is the second-highest district in the Sunless City.
The Anglerfish Overlook District serves as the main entrance from the Crash Site Caves trail.
A return trip from the Anglerfish Overlook District is often impossible due to falling sand.
A hidden Nomai scroll in the Anglerfish Overlook District reveals an easy method of reaching the Sun Station exists on Ash Twin.
The Stepping Stone District is the second-lowest district and contains ruined Nomai children's homes.
The Stepping Stone District connects to the Stepping Stone Cave: a large chamber with minimal footing and stepping-stone-like platforms.
The bottom of the Stepping Stone Cave leads to the High Energy Lab Trail.
The Stepping Stone Cave loops back to the Sunless City.
The Eye Shrine District is the highest district in the Sunless City and acts as a temple to the Eye of the Universe.
The Eye Shrine District contains information regarding the Nomai's search for the Eye of the Universe.
The Eye Shrine District's ground floor is filled with pockets of Ghost Matter.
A trail from the Eye Shrine District leads to the surface Gravity Cannon through cacti and Ghost Matter.
The High Energy Lab Trailhead is the lowest district in the Sunless City and marks the start of the trail to the High Energy Lab.
The High Energy Lab Trail is marked by a long energy cable snaking through the caverns.
The High Energy Lab Trail's first half is at the bottom of the Stepping Stone Cave.
The High Energy Lab Trail's second half is initially blocked by a powerful sandfall and a cactus field.
The Anglerfish Fossil is a large cavern containing a giant fossil of an Anglerfish.
The Anglerfish Fossil was called Fossil Fish Cave by Nomai children.
The Anglerfish Fossil has multiple viewing openings but only one entrance: a hidden crack on the ceiling found in the Stepping Stone Cave.
A gravity lift above the Anglerfish Fossil leads to a chamber with Nomai research on the fossil's blindness.
Ember Twin's Gravity Cannon is a huge cylindrical Nomai structure near the planet's equator.
The Ember Twin Gravity Cannon is linked to the Frozen Nomai Shuttle on the Interloper.
Recalling the Frozen Nomai Shuttle frees it from ice and allows access to its interior.
The High Energy Lab is an intact Nomai research facility built into Ember Twin's equatorial canyon.
The High Energy Lab is marked by a massive solar panel energy tower.
The High Energy Lab's main entrance is sealed from the inside.
The High Energy Lab's testing area has two input slots for spare black hole and white hole warp cores and a viewport large enough for a Scout to pass through.
The High Energy Lab's controls can redirect power between the Sunless City and the warp core testing area.
Chert's Camp is on a tall pillar at Ember Twin's north pole, in the center of a deep dry lakebed.
Chert's Camp has astronomy equipment and oxygen/jetpack refills.
The Quantum Caves are two Nomai cave entrances in the dry lakebed around Chert's Camp, opposite each other.
Each Quantum Cave entrance can contain the Cave Shard in a small chamber, depending on observation.
Quantum objects, including cacti, appear in proximity to the Cave Shard.
The Lakebed Cave is a deep winding cave at the very bottom of Ember Twin's north dry lakebed.
The Lakebed Cave fills with sand in the first minutes of each loop.
The first level of the Lakebed Cave is a maze with many paths blocked by stalactites.
Stalactites and cactus fields in the Lakebed Cave are quantum objects that disappear when unobserved.
A large chamber at the end of the Lakebed Cave maze is the third possible location of the Cave Shard.
Nomai writings in the Lakebed Cave reveal it as the location of Coleus's disappearance.
A fourth Cave Shard location is a hidden underground chamber with no entrances or exits, containing Coleus's musings after his rediscovery.
The Quantum Moon Locator is on the south pole of Ember Twin.
The Quantum Moon Locator has concentric rings with five symbols, each depicting a different celestial body in the solar system.
A fifth symbol on the Quantum Moon Locator shows the Moon's current orbit, moving to align with the corresponding body.
Ash Twin contains the Ash Twin Towers, a network of five teleporter towers built by the Nomai on a massive ring around Ash Twin's equator.
Each Ash Twin Tower visually represents the planet it connects to.
The five Ash Twin Towers warp to: Sun Station, Brittle Hollow, Giant's Deep, Timber Hearth, Ember Twin, and the Ash Twin Project.
The Sun Station Tower is shaped like a sun and is the tallest, the first to appear as sand recedes.
The path to the Sun Station Tower's warp platform is blocked by cacti late in the loop and must be traversed early through the sand.
The Giant's Deep Tower is shaped like a cyclone and connects to a warp receiver on Statue Island.
The Timber Hearth Tower is shaped like Geyser Mountain and connects to a warp receiver near the Nomai Mines; it contains trees for oxygen.
The Brittle Hollow Tower is shaped like a vertical section of the planet's crust and connects to the warp receiver in the Black Hole Forge District.
The Hourglass Twins tower is two towers with a bridge between them, representing the Twins and sand funnel.
The Hourglass Twins tower has two warp platforms (one for Ember Twin, one for Ash Twin Project), both activated when Ember Twin passes overhead.
The Ember Twin warp tower is larger and segmented in two, connecting to the warp receiver outside the High Energy Lab.
The Ash Twin Project warp tower is smaller and connects directly to a warp receiver inside the Ash Twin Project in the planet's core.
The Ash Twin Project tower has a broken ceiling that allows the sand funnel's pull to reach inside.
The Ash Twin Project is housed within an excavated shell at the core of Ash Twin.
Two solar panel energy towers stand at Ash Twin's north and south poles, connected to the Ash Twin Project.
lore: Annona, Coleus, Cycad, Oeno, Pye, Idaea, and other Nomai of Escape Pod 2 made their long-term shelter in the Sunless City after the Vessel crash.
Coleus and Melorae studied the Anglerfish Fossil in the Sunless City and discovered Anglerfish are blind and the specimen died from starvation.
Nomai children frequented the Stepping Stone District and used a secret crack-in-the-ceiling to enter the Anglerfish Fossil chamber.
Nomai writings in the Lakebed Cave chronicle the disappearance and rediscovery of Coleus, who discovered the new quantum-entanglement rule.
Coleus's quantum-entanglement rule: contacting a quantum object and ceasing observation (such as by entering complete darkness) allows one to travel with the quantum object.
The Nomai correctly surmised from the Quantum Moon Locator's gap that the Moon has a sixth location it can travel to.
Pye and Ramie were assigned to the High Energy Lab to recreate the negative time phenomenon first observed at the White Hole Station.
Ramie believed there was time warping going on, while Pye initially insisted it was equipment measurement error.
After rerouting Sunless City power to the Lab, Pye and Ramie proved the warps occurred before the actual departure, exciting both scientists.
The Southern Observatory's Nomai then asked whether the negative time interval could be increased to 22 minutes.
Extending the time interval required a more advanced warp core, much more space, and an exponentially larger energy source — becoming the basis of the Ash Twin Project.
The Ash Twin Tower network was designed at the High Energy Lab based on the White Hole Station, with five murals depicting the six tower designs.
Phlox is presumed to have designed the Ash Twin Towers based on the High Energy Lab plans.
The six warp cores inside the Ash Twin Towers were created at the Black Hole Forge.
The Nomai had intended to use the Ash Twin Project to discover the Eye of the Universe by pairing a Nomai Statue with the Orbital Probe Cannon's Probe Tracking Module.
The Nomai planned to artificially induce a supernova using the Sun Station to power the Ash Twin Project.
The Nomai's plan involved firing probes randomly, sending all probe data back 22 minutes via the Project, then selecting a new trajectory each loop until the Eye was found by chance.
When activated by the Nomai, the Sun Station failed to induce a supernova and the Project was put on hold.
The Ash Twin Project later activated accidentally when the Sun reached the natural end of its lifespan and supernovaed.
Chert at their north-pole camp gradually realizes over each loop that the universe is dying as stars supernova en masse.
mechanics: The Ash Twin Project is only accessible from the Ash Twin warp tower on Ash Twin's equator.
Removing the Ash Twin Project's Advanced Warp Core deactivates the Project and ends the time loop until reinserted.
Both Hourglass Twins tower platforms (Ember Twin and Ash Twin Project) activate simultaneously when Ember Twin passes overhead because the Twins share a center of gravity.
The Ash Twin Project warp tower's broken ceiling allows the sand funnel to suck the player out before the platform activates.
Reaching the Ash Twin Project requires sheltering under the adjoining bridge or hiding in the closet opposite the room during the sand pillar's center alignment.
Removing the Cave Shard's observation (by switching off the flashlight while standing on it) randomly teleports the Shard and the player to its fourth location.
The High Energy Lab's testing area produces a black hole and a white hole when paired warp cores are installed in the two slots.
Firing a Scout into the High Energy Lab's black hole causes it to exit the white hole slightly before entering the black hole.
Briefly two Scouts exist at once after firing, causing a Signal Duplication error.
Redirecting power from the Sunless City to the High Energy Lab experiment greatly pronounces the negative time effect.

Shooting a Scout at the High Energy Lab's black hole and removing the black hole core before the Scout actually enters the black hole creates a temporal paradox and triggers the Breaking Spacetime Ending.
Recalling the Frozen Nomai Shuttle from the Interloper to Ember Twin's Gravity Cannon allows entry to its interior.
Hiding under the Hourglass Twins tower's adjoining bridge protects the player from the sand funnel's pull during alignment.
Autopilot is not recommended near the Twins due to risk of crashing into the Sun or one of the Twins.
